metadata.title: The Jobs Nobody Could Find
metadata.note: deep-explainer documentary built from a 12-week OPT ship log (addams.pdf, Humanitarians.ai / Jobsekr). Three acts: the visa-classification pipeline (wk 1-2), the technical-SEO system (wk 3-8), getting indexed + the honest transition-week coda (wk 9-12). Teardown register, narrated by Bella for Humanitarians AI. NO IN-FOR-BEAR LAW: this cut signs in and off as Humanitarians AI, not Liam-in-for-Bear. Slate previz first (Gate D1). Never publishes. Narration is spoken from narration_text.

beats.narration_text: There's a twelve-week ship log for a job board here — and this is Humanitarians AI. Twenty-three thousand real job listings that, for most of that stretch, no international student could actually find. Today we take apart the two systems that changed that: one that reads a job for visa signal, one that makes the page exist for Google. And we do not skip the week where it didn't work.

props.command: Here's a 12-week engineering ship log for a job board. Walk me through the two systems that turned 23,000 inert listings into a live, searchable product — a visa classifier and an SEO stack — and show me exactly where the log is honest about what did NOT ship.
output: system one: a five-tier visa classifier
system two: an SEO stack for 23K pages
the coda: the week it stalled — reported straight

beats.narration_text: Act one. The inert database — correct code that no user had ever actually felt.

props.headline: Act one. The inert database — correct code that no user…

beats.narration_text: Start with the failure, not the win. The classifier existed and passed its tests — but the migration had never run in production. So every one of twenty-three thousand listings carried the same thing for a visa tag: nothing.

props.headline: Start with the failure, not the win. The classifier existed and…

beats.narration_text: Week one flips it live. An idempotent migration — every statement guarded by if-not-exists — adds the columns and the indexes. A merged workflow then starts the classifier on a fifteen-minute cron, with its secrets resolved against production.

props.title: 003_visa_tags.sql — idempotent, safe to re-run
props.sparkLine: Every statement guarded — the migration is re-runnable by design.

beats.narration_text: Then the backfill. Page the unclassified jobs a thousand at a time, tag each one, and write back by group — no row-by-row updates. Twenty-three thousand listings classified for the first time, in under two minutes.

props.headline: Then the backfill. Page the unclassified jobs a thousand at a…

beats.narration_text: Fast is not the same as right. So before anyone trusts it, the tag distribution gets graded — expected ranges per tier, plus two blunt sanity checks: no US job left untagged, and no foreign job wearing a visa tag.

props.headline: Fast is not the same as right. So before anyone trusts…

beats.narration_text: Four tiers read the job description. The fifth reads the company. A listing with no visa language, posted by an employer with a real sponsorship history, becomes a signal instead of a shrug — no-data turned into maybe.

props.headline: Four tiers read the job description. The fifth reads the company.…

beats.narration_text: The dangerous part is the join, so the rule is deliberately narrow: only ever promote jobs already tagged no-data. A description that already said something always wins. Company history can add information — it can never overwrite it.

props.headline: The dangerous part is the join, so the rule is deliberately…

beats.narration_text: Five tiers, feature-complete. The database can finally answer the one question the whole audience is actually asking: will this place sponsor me.

props.headline: Five tiers, feature-complete. The database can finally answer the one question…

beats.narration_text: Act two. Invisible to Google — because a tagged job nobody can find is still a job nobody found.

props.headline: Act two. Invisible to Google — because a tagged job nobody…

beats.narration_text: The jobs were classified and still unreachable. Google for Jobs sits above normal search and runs entirely on structured data. Without it, twenty-three thousand pages were invisible to the single biggest way people actually arrive.

props.headline: The jobs were classified and still unreachable. Google for Jobs sits…

beats.narration_text: So every job page learns to describe itself. A structured-data block maps the listing onto the schema Google reads — title, dates, employer, location — with salary and remote handling when the data exists, and safe defaults when it doesn't.

props.headline: So every job page learns to describe itself. A structured-data block…

beats.narration_text: Structured data off the page is useless, so it's wired into the page itself. Canonical URLs kill the duplicate a modal would create. Expired jobs get no-index. And one robots file opens the public routes while closing the private ones.

props.headline: Structured data off the page is useless, so it's wired into…

beats.narration_text: Then a map for the crawler. A sitemap index points to four children — jobs, companies, landing pages, and static — each capped and shardable past fifty thousand. Only active listings go in, so Google never spends crawl budget on dead pages.

props.headline: Then a map for the crawler. A sitemap index points to…

beats.narration_text: Generic pages don't rank for 'H-1B jobs in Seattle.' So thirty cities cross fifteen roles into dozens of pages built for that exact search — each one server-rendered with live counts and real sponsors, never thin, duplicate filler.

props.headline: Generic pages don't rank for 'H-1B jobs in Seattle.' So thirty…

beats.narration_text: Templated pages look identical to Google, and identical reads as a penalty. Per-page questions and answers, varied by city and role, give each page its own snippet-eligible content — and its own defense against being filed as a duplicate.

props.headline: Templated pages look identical to Google, and identical reads as a…

beats.narration_text: Structured data, canonicals, sitemaps, landing pages, snippets — the whole surface shipped. But shipping SEO and actually ranking are two different weeks.

props.headline: Structured data, canonicals, sitemaps, landing pages, snippets — the whole surface…

beats.narration_text: Act three. Getting seen — honestly. This is where the log stops flattering itself.

props.headline: Act three. Getting seen — honestly. This is where the log…

beats.narration_text: The system finally meets Google. The domain is verified, every sitemap submitted and accepted, the highest-value pages pushed for indexing. Coverage and impressions start to show up — and so, right beside them, do the warnings.

props.headline: The system finally meets Google. The domain is verified, every sitemap…

beats.narration_text: So there's an audit pass. Lighthouse on real job and landing pages until they clear ninety. The structured-data warnings — missing recommended fields, answers that looked too alike — get fixed at the root and re-validated, not muted.

props.headline: So there's an audit pass. Lighthouse on real job and landing…

beats.narration_text: Then the whole chain gets walked once, end to end: a freshly scraped job detected as US, classified into a tier, rendered as a valid structured page, listed in the sitemap, and visible in Search Console. It holds.

props.headline: Then the whole chain gets walked once, end to end: a…

beats.narration_text: Code without documentation is a liability the day its author leaves. So both systems get written down — the tiers and their order, the sitemap tree, the audit loop — and handed off, so someone else can run them without the person who built them.

props.headline: Code without documentation is a liability the day its author leaves.…

beats.narration_text: And then the log does the rare thing. The next assignment stalls — no repository access, no task, hours below the bar — and the report says exactly that, instead of padding the week. A ship log you can trust is one that records the weeks it didn't ship.

props.headline: And then the log does the rare thing. The next assignment…

beats.narration_text: The verdict, one page. Two systems: a five-tier classifier that turns a listing into a visa signal, and an SEO stack that turns a page into something Google can find. One backfill — twenty-three thousand jobs, under two minutes. And one rule that keeps both honest: information gets added, never overwritten — in the data, and in the log.

props.artifactTitle: The Jobs Nobody Could Find — one page
artifactLines: System 1: a five-tier visa classifier — four tiers read the description, the fifth reads the company's sponsorship history.
System 2: an SEO stack — JSON-LD, canonical/noindex, a sharded sitemap tree, data-backed landing pages, per-page FAQ snippets.
The run: one backfill classified 23,000 listings in under two minutes; end-to-end verified scrape → tag → indexable page.
The rule: information is added, never overwritten — no-data-only promotion in the data, and an honest coda in the log.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Take your own project's ship log and run one prompt on it: for every week, separate what actually reached production from what was only written or planned — and make it name the weeks that fell short. No spin. No verdict without a receipt.

props.command: Here's my project's weekly ship log. For every week, separate what actually shipped to production from what was only drafted or planned, flag any week that fell short of its hours or goals, and cite the specific commit, PR, or artifact for each 'shipped' claim. No receipt, no credit.

beats.narration_text: The jobs nobody could find. If a build log that tells the truth is worth more to you than one that only wins, subscribe. Humanitarians AI.
